correctness.summary: Distinct members cannot be tangent because a point-hyperplane pair determines a unique leaf. The parameter tangent space gives a complete normal first-jet system on a fixed member; in the two-sided case its normalized basis map is a diffeomorphism to S^n, and on the one-sided normal orientation cover it is antipodal-equivariant and descends to RP^n. Thus nearby pair intersections are standard S^{n-1} or RP^{n-1} zero sets. The total pair-incidence projection over the punctured parameter space is a proper submersion; its image is nonempty, open, and closed, and the base is connected. Ehresmann's theorem then forces every pair to intersect with the same diffeomorphism and isotopy type.

limitations: Only unoriented transitive families of closed embedded hypersurfaces in dimensions at least three are covered.
Arbitrary oriented transitive families are excluded; standard oriented examples may contain disjoint members.
No theorem about triple or higher multiple intersections is claimed.
No quantitative intersection-angle or metric stability estimate is obtained.
The n=1 case is not treated.
The motivating preprint is very recent, so later revisions or unindexed parallel observations may overlap.
Independent audit has not been performed.

originality.summary: Martins' 2026 preprint classifies the ambient manifold and individual hypersurface topology and supplies the double-fibration/normal-variation structure, but no theorem classifying all pairwise intersections or the proper pair-incidence bundle was located. Searches over equivalent terminology involving hypersurface Zoll and transitive families, pairwise intersections, incidence, transversality, spheres, and projective hyperplanes, together with the main construction and transitive-family sources, did not locate the stated result. The motivating preprint is extremely recent, so a later revision or unindexed parallel observation remains the principal residual risk.

value.summary: The theorem upgrades individual topological classification to a global incidence law: every distinct pair meets, the intersection is transverse and connected, and its topology cannot bifurcate. The fiber-bundle formulation organizes all intersections with a fixed member. For hypersurface Zoll manifolds this recovers the incidence pattern of great spheres and projective hyperplanes; in dimension three every two distinct Zoll minimal surfaces meet in a single embedded circle.
